summary:
The hitting category is the story of the model right now, and it's scorching across every rating: R1 at 64% (18-10, n=28, +13.6pts), R2 at 68% (+18.6pts), R3 at 68% (+18.4pts), and R4 leading the pack at a ridiculous 75% (21-7, +22.8pts over its 52% season mark). Bullpen_fatigue is right behind it, hot on all four ratings (R1-R3 at +14.2pts, R4 at +15.2pts), though note all four carry a 3L streak in that same window — hot doesn't mean currently winning every night, it means the recent sample is outperforming baseline. The real red flag is SP: every rating is cold there, 13-15 (46%) over the last 14 days with a brutal 7L streak running across R1 through R4, a 6-9 point drag below season norms. If a pick is leaning on starting pitching grades alone today, fade that confidence.

Today's slate is a single game, but it's a clean one: CLE @ TBR, and all four ratings agree on CLE, with deltas ranging from R1's -1.22 down to R3's -0.86 — full consensus with no daylight between the models. TBR as a team-when-liked play has been excellent for the model historically (42-19, 69%, n=61, +21.0u in strong spots), so backing against TBR here runs counter to one of the stronger team trends in the sample — worth weighing against the consensus lean toward CLE. Context matters: Freddy Peralta on the mound for TBR means the model's SP grade is in play, and SP is the coldest category in the shop right now (46% last 14, 7L streak), which could be dragging CLE's number lower than it deserves if the model is overweighting a cold signal. With only one game on the board, there's no diversification — if this is a strong-play threshold bet, recent 30-day strong-play returns are still strong across the board (R1 +25.0u, R3 +21.0u at 69%), but the 7-day window has gone cold for every rating except R1, so size accordingly and don't chase the full season number on a single-game slate.
